hero.srTitle: Romain Kantzer, web developer in Alsace: business websites, online stores, web applications and mobile apps.
hero.lead: I design, code and launch websites and apps for small businesses and associations. Then I show you how to run them yourself.
hero.ruleCenter: From Alsace to the rest of the web

about.label: Who I am
about.text: My name is Romain. I'm an engineer, and I build websites and apps for small businesses and associations. I explain what I do without jargon, I take care of the whole technical side, and you stay in control of your tool. *One person to talk to, from the first conversation to launch.*

facts.label: I work

project.label: Project
project.title: Cercle d'Échecs de *Bischwiller*
project.text: The club's website was more than fifteen years old. I rebuilt it completely, then trained the volunteers so they could publish their own news. Today the club keeps its website alive without me.

site-vitrine.name: Business website
site-vitrine.title: Business *website*
site-vitrine.short: To present your business, be found on Google and receive enquiries.
site-vitrine.lead: A website that clearly explains what you do, where to find you and how to get in touch. It's often the first contact a customer has with you: it needs to be clear, fast and up to date.

included.title: The design and the copy, with you
included.text: We build the page structure and the content together. I help you write what your customers are really looking for.

included.title: Readable on every screen
included.text: Phone, tablet, computer: every page is designed to be readable everywhere.

included.title: The basics of local SEO
included.text: Titles, descriptions, markup and sitemap: the essentials so Google understands who you are and where you work.

included.title: A contact form straight to your inbox
included.text: Enquiries reach you directly, with no extra tool to keep an eye on.

included.title: A space to edit your content
included.text: News, opening hours, photos: you update them yourself, and I show you how.

included.title: Domain name, hosting, launch
included.text: I handle the technical side, from choosing the address to putting the site online.

build.text: I build websites with Next.js and React: pages load quickly and the code stays easy to evolve. If you need to publish often, I add a simple editing tool so you stay in control.

faq.q: How much does a business website cost?
faq.a: It depends on the number of pages, the content to produce and the features. After a first conversation, I send you a detailed, line-by-line quote so you know exactly what you're paying for.

faq.q: I don't have any copy or photos yet — is that a problem?
faq.a: No. We start from what you have and I help you structure the rest. I tell you clearly what to prepare, and when.

faq.q: Will I be able to edit the site myself?
faq.a: Yes, that's the whole point. I train you to update your content, just as I did with the volunteers of the Bischwiller chess club.

faq.q: I already have a website — can you rebuild it?
faq.a: Yes. I keep the useful content, keep your domain name and make sure the old addresses redirect to the new pages.

site-e-commerce.name: Online store
site-e-commerce.title: Online *store*
site-e-commerce.short: To sell your products online, take payments and follow your orders.
site-e-commerce.lead: An online store where customers find your products, pay securely and get a confirmation, while you manage orders from a single place.
forWho: Shops that want to sell beyond their storefront
Associations selling memberships, tickets or merchandise

included.title: A clear catalogue
included.text: Product pages with photos, variants (size, colour…), stock and prices, easy to update.

included.title: Secure online payment
included.text: Card and common payment methods, through a recognised provider such as Stripe. No card details pass through your site.

included.title: Shipping and pickup
included.text: Shipping rates by zone, in-store pickup or click & collect: we set up what fits the way you work.

included.title: Order emails
included.text: Confirmation, shipping, invoice: your customers are kept informed at every step, automatically.

included.title: A back office to manage it all
included.text: Orders, customers, stock: you follow everything from a simple interface, and I show you how to use it.

included.title: The mandatory pages
included.text: I plan the legal pages (terms of sale, legal notice, privacy policy) and integrate them from your texts.

build.text: Depending on the size of your catalogue and your needs, I suggest either a ready-made platform such as Shopify, handy if you want to run the store on your own day to day, or a store coded with Next.js and Stripe, with more freedom and no platform subscription. I explain the difference before we start, in terms of cost as well as use.

faq.q: Shopify or a custom-coded store: which should I choose?
faq.a: Shopify works well if you want a ready-made platform with a monthly subscription. A store coded with Next.js gives you more freedom over design and features, with no platform subscription (only the payment provider's fees apply). I help you choose based on your catalogue and budget.

faq.q: Who takes care of photos and product pages?
faq.a: You know your products better than I do: you provide the information, I build clear product pages and show you how to add new ones. If you have a lot of products, we plan an import.

faq.q: Can I start small?
faq.a: Yes. We can launch the store with a few products and grow it afterwards. It's often the best way to see what works before investing more.

faq.q: How are payments handled?
faq.a: By a recognised payment provider such as Stripe. It handles card security; the money is paid directly into your account.

application-web.name: Web application
application-web.title: Web *application*
application-web.short: To replace your spreadsheets, manage bookings or open a client area.
application-web.lead: An online tool designed around the way you work: bookings, client area, member management, scheduling, quotes… Available from a browser, nothing to install.
forWho: Associations managing members, sign-ups or schedules
Professionals who want an online client area
Founders who want to test an idea

included.title: We start from your day-to-day
included.text: I look at how you work today before suggesting anything. The application should simplify, not add another layer.

included.title: Accounts and access
included.text: Secure login and roles (administrator, member, client): everyone sees what concerns them.

included.title: Your data in one place
included.text: A clean database replaces scattered files. You can export your data whenever you want.

included.title: Useful notifications
included.text: Confirmation emails, reminders, alerts: the application notifies the right people at the right time.

included.title: A first version you can use early
included.text: We start with the essentials so you can use it early, then add what's really missing.

included.title: Hosting and follow-up
included.text: I put the application online, keep an eye on it and apply the security updates.

build.text: I use Next.js and React for the interface, and a PostgreSQL database (often through Supabase) to store your information and manage accounts. These are widely used tools: you're not locked in with me.

faq.q: What's the difference between a website and a web application?
faq.a: A website presents information. An application lets people act: book, manage, log in, save data. Many projects mix both.

faq.q: How long does it take to build an application?
faq.a: It all depends on the number of features. That's why I suggest starting with a first version limited to the essentials: you get a usable tool sooner, and a precise schedule with the quote.

faq.q: Is my data safe?
faq.a: Access is protected by authentication, exchanges are encrypted and data is hosted in Europe whenever possible. I explain where it's stored and who can access it.

faq.q: What if I need a mobile app later?
faq.a: A web application can already be used on a phone. If you need a real app in the stores, much of the work can be reused.

application-mobile.name: Mobile app
application-mobile.title: Mobile *app*
application-mobile.short: To be in your customers' or your team's pocket, on iPhone and Android.
application-mobile.lead: An app installed on the phones of your customers, members or team, on iPhone and Android. Notifications, quick access, use in the field: for when a website is no longer enough.
forWho: Shops that want to build customer loyalty
Clubs and associations that want to keep members informed
Projects that need the phone's features: camera, location, notifications

included.title: One app for iPhone and Android
included.text: I develop with React Native: one codebase for both systems, which means lower costs and simpler updates.

included.title: Screens designed for thumbs
included.text: Simple navigation, readable text, natural gestures: the app should make sense without a manual.

included.title: Notifications
included.text: Reminders, news, messages: you reach your users directly on their phone.

included.title: A connected back office
included.text: You manage content and users from a web interface, without touching the code.

included.title: Publishing in the stores
included.text: I prepare the App Store and Google Play listings and guide you through Apple's and Google's review.

included.title: Follow-up after launch
included.text: OS updates, fixes, new features: the app keeps living.

build.text: I build apps with React Native and Expo, in the same language as my websites. Data and accounts rely on the same kind of database as my web applications, so a website, a web app and a mobile app can share the same information.

faq.q: Do I really need a mobile app?
faq.a: Not always. If your users mainly need to look up information, a well-made website is enough. An app makes sense when it's opened often, or when you need notifications and the phone's features. I'll tell you honestly in our first conversation.

faq.q: Do I need Apple and Google developer accounts?
faq.a: Yes, the app is published under your name. Apple charges an annual fee, Google a one-off payment. I guide you through the process.

faq.q: How long does store review take?
faq.a: It depends on Apple and Google. I plan for this step in the schedule and handle the exchanges with them if changes are requested.

faq.q: Can you take over an existing app?
faq.a: It depends on the technology used. I look at the code before committing and tell you clearly what's possible.

servicesPage.label: Services
servicesPage.title: Websites and apps, *from A to Z*.
servicesPage.lead: I take care of everything, from the first conversation to launch: planning, design, development, hosting. You have one person to talk to, who knows your project inside out.

faq.q: Do you only work in Alsace?
faq.a: I'm based in Rountzenheim, in the Bas-Rhin, and I'm happy to travel around the region to meet. I also work remotely, by video call, with clients further away.

faq.q: How does the quote work?
faq.a: After a free first conversation, I send you a detailed quote: what's included, what isn't, and the schedule. You know exactly what you're paying for.

faq.q: Will my site rank well?
faq.a: I take care of the technical SEO basics on every project: page structure, loading speed, tags, sitemap. Ranking also depends on your content and competition: I explain how to work on it over time, without promising you first place.

faq.q: Do you offer maintenance?
faq.a: Yes. After launch, I can keep handling updates, security and improvements. We discuss it when preparing the quote, based on your needs.

faq.q: I don't know which solution to choose — can you help?
faq.a: That's exactly what the first conversation is for. You describe your needs, and I tell you honestly what seems right, including when a simpler solution will do.

process.label: How it works
process.title: From the first conversation to *launch*.
process.intro: Every project follows the same steps. You always know where things stand and what comes next.

steps.title: We *talk*
steps.text: A free first conversation, by phone, video call or in person. You tell me about your business and what you expect. I tell you honestly what seems useful, and what doesn't.

steps.title: The *mock-up*
steps.text: Before writing a single line of code, I show you what the project will look like, screen by screen. We adjust together until it's right.

steps.title: The *build*
steps.text: I code the website or app. You follow progress on an online preview you can check at any time, and send me feedback as we go.

steps.title: The *launch*
steps.text: Domain name, hosting, store publishing for a mobile app: I take care of it all. Then I train you so you're independent.

steps.title: And *after*
steps.text: I stay reachable. Updates, security, new features: we keep going together if you'd like.

cta.label: Contact
cta.title: Let's talk about *your project*.
cta.text: A website, a store, an app? Tell me what you have in mind, even if it's not very precise yet. I'll reply personally.

story.label: My story
story.title: Who I *am*
story.p1: I come from Rountzenheim, a village in northern Alsace. I trained in industrial automation, then earned my engineering degree in digital solutions at Icam Strasbourg-Europe, as an apprentice at ERAS.
story.quote: I learned to build things that have to work every day, not just on demo day.
story.p2: It all started with my chess club in Bischwiller. Its website was more than fifteen years old. I rebuilt it completely: new design, content carried over, domain name and hosting — and above all, I trained the volunteers so they could publish their own news. Today the club keeps its website alive without me.
story.p3: That project made me want to turn this into my job. I created RK.ai to bring the same thing to small businesses and associations around here: clear websites and apps that look like them, and that they can keep alive themselves.

items.title: No jargon
items.text: I explain what I do and why, in plain words. You always know what you are paying for.

items.title: You stay independent
items.text: I train your team or your volunteers to publish without me, just like I did with the chess club.

items.title: I handle the technical side
items.text: Domain name, hosting, maintenance: I take care of that part so you never have to think about it.

items.title: I'm local
items.text: I work from Rountzenheim and I'm happy to meet in person to talk things over.
